children: Airline major IndiGo’s share of India’s domestic air passenger market slipped in August 2026, while the Air India Group gained ground, even as overall passenger traffic declined y-o-y.

According to data released by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), IndiGo carried 78.87 lakh passengers during August 2026, accounting for 65 per cent of the market, down from 67.4 per cent in July.
The Air India Group, comprising Air India and Air India Express, increased its combined market share to 26.7 per cent from 24 per cent in July after carrying 32.32 lakh passengers.

Meanwhile, Akasa Air held its market share steady at 5.5 per cent after carrying 6.68 lakh passengers, while SpiceJet’s share fell further to 1.2 per cent. Star Air, Fly91 and Alliance Air accounted for 0.7 per cent, 0.5 per cent and 0.5 per cent, respectively.

Overall, scheduled domestic airlines carried around 1.21 crore passengers during August 2026, compared with around 1.29 crore passengers during the corresponding period of last year, a y-o-y decline of about 6.3 per cent.
On a sequential basis, traffic rose marginally from around 1.20 crore passengers in July.

For the January–August 2026 period, domestic airlines carried around 11.05 crore passengers, compared with 11.07 crore passengers during the corresponding period of last year, a marginal decline of 0.18 per cent.

Speaking to businessline, industry observers said that traffic remained largely flat sequentially during the lean monsoon travel season, with passenger load factors declining across most airlines during August compared with July.

On the other hand, Akasa Air recorded the highest passenger load factor during August 2026 at 87.6 per cent, followed by SpiceJet (79.9 per cent), IndiGo (79.2 per cent) and the Air India Group (77.0 per cent).
Besides, Fly91 and IndiaOne Air were the only carriers to improve their load factors during the month, at 75.0 per cent and 47.5 per cent, respectively.

Furthermore, the overall cancellation rate of scheduled domestic airlines during August 2026 stood at 1.04 per cent, with technical reasons accounting for about half of all cancellations at 50.2 per cent, followed by operational reasons (20.4 per cent), miscellaneous reasons (17.4 per cent) and weather-related disruptions (8.5 per cent).

Additionally, SpiceJet recorded the highest cancellation rate at 20.92 per cent, followed by IndiaOne Air (10.60 per cent) and Alliance Air (4.58 per cent), while Akasa Air recorded the lowest at 0.07 per cent.
In all, 67,462 passengers were affected by cancellations during the month, with airlines spending around ₹93.78 lakh on facilitation and compensation.

For on-time performance at ten major airports, IndiGo led at 91.5 per cent, followed by Akasa Air (90.5 per cent) and the Air India Group (83.9 per cent), while Alliance Air stood at 71.8 per cent and SpiceJet trailed at 17.9 per cent.

In addition, scheduled domestic airlines received 2,132 passenger complaints during August, or around 1.76 complaints per 10,000 passengers, with baggage-related issues accounting for the largest share at 29.5 per cent.

title: IndiGo’s market share slips in August as Air India Group gains
